'''Komori Shrine''' (子守神社, also read as Komamori Jinja) refers to various {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}}s across Japan. As the name suggests, these shrines enshrine the "Komori no Kami" (child-protecting deity) and serve as protectors of children. They may be enshrined as the primary deity ([[ujigami]]) or as subsidiary shrines within larger shrine precincts. The name can also be written as 籠守 or 子護.

Komori shrines are associated with two main lineages: the [[Mikumari|Mikumari-no-Kami]] lineage and the lineage of the eighth shrine of [[Kumano Hongū Taisha]].

== Lineages ==
=== Mikumari-no-Kami Lineage ===
Mikumari-no-Kami, originally a [[:en:Water deity|Water deity]] responsible for water distribution, came to be associated with child protection as the pronunciation of "Mikumari" (みくまり) shifted to "Mikomori" (御子守), meaning child protection. The head shrine of this lineage is {{ill|Yoshino Mikumari Shrine|en|Yoshino Mikumari Shrine|qid=Q3529714|lt=Yoshino Mikumari Shrine}} in {{ill|Yoshino, Nara|en|Yoshino, Nara|qid=Q1203731|lt=Yoshino, Nara}}.

=== Kumano Hongū Taisha Lineage ===
The eighth shrine of Kumano Hongū Taisha, known as Komori-no-Miya, enshrines a deity referred to in the {{ill|Ryōjin Hishō|en|Ryōjin Hishō|qid=Q3010584|lt=Ryōjin Hishō}}: "The children of the gods, such as the Wakamiya of Hachiman and the Wakōji and Komori Gozen of Kumano." Shrines in this lineage include the subsidiary {{ill|Kusu Shrine (Komori Shrine)|ja|楠神社}} of {{ill|Fujishiro Ōji Shrine|lt=Fujishiro Ōji|lt=Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujishiro Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q3090605}} in {{ill|Kainan, Wakayama|en|Kainan, Wakayama|qid=Q841309|lt=Kainan, Wakayama}}.

Additional associations include {{ill|Isagawa Shrine|ja|率川神社}} in {{ill|Nara (city)|en|Nara (city)|qid=Q169134|lt=Nara City}}, which is also known as Komori Myōjin.
